title: Signature Lineage-Weighted Consensus
description: Signature edition: every ballot carries the voter's Signature lineage stamp, and votes are weighted by verified lineage depth — models with longer audited track records count more. Ballots are journaled so any consensus can be replayed and audited vote by vote. This is a Signature original method.
method: Each agent signs its ballot with its lineage stamp; weight = f(verified lineage depth, task calibration); the journal records ballot, weight, and tally for replay.
usage: Issue lineage stamps to each agent, configure the weighting function, and journal every round.

title: Signature Multi-agent debate rounds
description: Signature edition: In the debate protocol (Du et al.), several model instances propose answers, then read each other's reasoning and revise over multiple rounds before a judge (or vote) picks the winner. Debate surfaces hidden flaws: agents must defend claims against critics, which measurably improves factuality on hard questions.
method: Round 0: each agent answers independently. Rounds 1..k: each agent sees peers' answers and critiques them, then revises. Final: majority vote or a separate judge model selects.

specification.paper: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in LLMs through Multiagent Debate (Du et al., 2023)

usage: Use for high-stakes answers: spawn 3 debaters with different system prompts, run 2 critique rounds, then judge.

demo.code:
agents = {'A': 'Paris', 'B': 'Paris', 'C': 'London'}
print('round 0:', agents)
agents['C'] = 'Paris'  # C concedes after reading A's evidence
print('round 1 after critique:', agents)
print('final: Paris by 3/3')

title: Signature Condorcet pairwise ranking
description: Signature edition: When models rank multiple candidate answers, Condorcet voting compares every pair head-to-head: the candidate beating all others pairwise wins. It avoids vote-splitting pathologies of simple plurality when several similar good answers divide the vote.
method: Each agent submits a ranking; build the pairwise matrix (how many agents prefer X over Y); the Condorcet winner beats every rival; fall back to ranked-pairs if a cycle appears.
usage: Use when choosing among several plausible outputs (summaries, designs); collect rankings, compute the matrix, declare the winner.

demo.code:
import itertools
rankings = [['A','B','C'], ['A','C','B'], ['B','A','C']]
cands = ['A','B','C']
for x, y in itertools.combinations(cands, 2):
    xy = sum(1 for r in rankings if r.index(x) < r.index(y))
    print(f'{x} over {y}: {xy}-{len(rankings)-xy}')
print('A beats B 2-1 and C 3-0 -> Condorcet winner: A')

title: Signature Byzantine-tolerant agent quorum
description: Signature edition: Borrowed from distributed systems: with up to f malicious or faulty agents, 3f+1 agents and 2f+1 agreeing votes guarantee a correct decision. Applied to LLM teams, it bounds how many hallucinating or compromised agents the consensus can survive — relevant when agents come from untrusted sources.
method: Agents commit to answers (hash reveal), then reveal; a decision needs 2f+1 matching reveals; equivocating agents are slashed from the pool.
usage: Use when agents are untrusted or independently operated; keep f small (1-2) since cost scales with n.

demo.code:
agents = ['A-ok', 'B-ok', 'C-byzantine', 'D-ok']
votes = ['yes', 'yes', 'no', 'yes']
print('agents:', agents)
print('2f+1 quorum with f=1 needs 3 matching ->', 'yes' if votes.count('yes') >= 3 else 'no')

title: Signature Stacked generalization of model outputs
description: Signature edition: Stacking trains a meta-model on the outputs of base models: each base LLM answers, and a small classifier or regressor learns which model to trust for which inputs. Unlike fixed weights, the meta-learner adapts trust by input features — model A for math, model B for prose.
method: Collect base-model answers on a labeled set; featurize (task type, answer length, model confidences); train the meta-model; at inference, base models run in parallel and the meta-model picks or blends.
usage: Build the labeled set from past judgments; retrain the meta-model as base models change.

demo.code:
print('stacking decision table:')
table = [('math', 'trust model A (0.94 math acc)'), ('prose', 'trust model B (0.91 prose acc)')]
for task, rule in table:
    print(f'  {task:6} -> {rule}')
print('meta-model routes per input features.')

title: Signature CRDT merge of partial agent drafts
description: Signature edition: When agents draft different sections of one document, conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) merge their edits without a central arbiter. Each agent works on its own replica; the merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent — order of arrival never changes the result.
method: Represent the draft as a CRDT (e.g., Yjs/YATA for text, OR-Set for lists); agents apply local ops; replicas sync and merge deterministically; final document is the join of all ops.
usage: Give each agent a replica of the shared doc, let them edit concurrently, and sync on a timer or on demand.

title: Signature Weighted voting by model calibration
description: Signature edition: Not all models are equal: weighted voting gives each model's ballot a weight from its historical accuracy or calibration score on similar tasks. A small accurate specialist can outvote two mediocre generalists, which plain majority vote cannot express.
method: Maintain per-model, per-task-type accuracy from past judgments; weight = log(accuracy/(1-accuracy)) (log-odds); the answer with the highest summed weight wins.
usage: Log every model's verdicts with ground truth when available; recompute weights nightly; apply at consensus time.

demo.code:
votes = [('A', 'yes', 0.9), ('B', 'no', 0.7), ('C', 'no', 0.6)]
import math
score = {}
for m, v, acc in votes:
    w = math.log(acc / (1 - acc))
    score[v] = score.get(v, 0) + w
print('weighted scores:', {k: round(x, 2) for k, x in score.items()})
print('winner:', max(score, key=score.get))

title: Signature Mixture-of-Agents layering
description: Signature edition: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) stacks layers of diverse LLMs: each layer's models see all previous-layer outputs and refine them, with a final aggregator producing the answer. Like MoE for whole models, it exploits that different models have different strengths, and open models in MoA layers have matched or beaten GPT-4 on benchmarks.
method: Layer 1: n proposer models generate drafts. Layers 2..k: each model receives concatenated prior outputs as context and refines. Final aggregator synthesizes.

specification.result: open models rivaling flagship on AlpacaEval

usage: Configure 2-3 proposer models per layer, 2 layers, and one strong aggregator; cache aggressively since cost multiplies.

demo.code:
layer1 = ['draft A: 15%', 'draft B: 0.15', 'draft C: 15 percent']
print('proposers:', layer1)
agg = 'Consensus: 15% (0.15) — all three drafts agree.'
print('aggregator:', agg)

title: Signature LLM-as-judge scoring panel
description: Signature edition: Instead of voting on identical outputs, a judge model scores candidate answers against a rubric (correctness, completeness, clarity). Panels of judges — or one judge with a strict rubric — pick winners in generation tournaments, RLHF data curation, and eval harnesses like MT-Bench.
method: Candidates are presented pairwise or listwise to the judge with a scoring rubric; judges output scores plus rationales; the top scorer wins, with position-bias mitigation by swapping candidate order.
usage: Define the rubric first, run each candidate through the judge twice (orders swapped), and average.

demo.code:
cands = {'A': 8.5, 'B': 7.0, 'C': 9.0}
winner = max(cands, key=cands.get)
print('judge scores:', cands)
print('winner:', winner, '-> selected for output')
